thread:
nina: Seeing a sharp latency spike in eu-central around 21:15 UTC, p50 -> p95s jumped and GPU hotpool utilization hit 98%
ryan: Confirmed in metrics, batching queue depth exploded. Looks like many requests landed on a small subset of workers.
stefan: KV-cache eviction rate also spiked at the same time, lots of hotlocks in runtime logs. suspect k/v lock thrash after last runtime bump.
maria: Any recent deploys in eu? I saw a runtime build rolled out ~20:50 UTC.
nina: @deploy-bot shows runtime v2.14.3 canary -> prod at 20:47 UTC (eu).
infra-bot: Alert: eu-central provisioning failures x 6 in past 10m (api error 503), autoscaler backoff engaged.
ryan: Autoscaler backoff + hotpool saturation = no new GPUs to relieve overloaded workers.
oncall-lead: Prioritize traffic diversion to na1/na2 and spin emergency hotpool in eu if possible. Cost > latency for now.
stefan: Quick plan: 1) divert non-critical customer traffic to na1 2) restart provisioner control-plane in eu 3) patch runtime to revert the KV eviction change if needed.
maria: Divert rule ready. I'll shift preview and internal traffic first. Command: `./trafficctl shift --from eu-central --to na1 --filter 'tier!=prod'`
nina: Doing the shift now for non-prod.
infra-bot: Traffic shift executed: 42% of non-prod requests diverted to na1.
ryan: Non-prod latency back to normal, but prod still elevated and hotpool still saturated.
stefan: Can we scale up a temporary cold-gpu pool in eu? We have spare quota but autoscaler backoff blocks creation. Trying manual provision.
maria: Manual provision command: `provisioner create --region eu-central --pool temp-hotpool --gpu A100-40GB --count 6`
infra-bot: Provision request accepted, but nodes failing healthcheck due to `kv-attach-timeout` in runtime logs.
oncall-lead: That suggests runtime change is preventing new nodes from completing init. Revert runtime?
stefan: I can push a rollback to previous runtime v2.14.1 in eu only. Would take ~6m to drain and restart. Approve?
ryan: Approve for eu-only rollback. Also add a temporary rate limit on heavy routes to reduce queue pressure: `rlctl set /v1/generate  qps=20`
nina: Rollback started. Deploy-bot: started rollback of runtime to v2.14.1 in eu-central (canary window off).
deploy-bot: rollback in progress — 3/12 hosts restarted. No errors so far.
stefan: After 2/3 of hosts rolled back, kv-attach-timeout errors stop on new nodes. Hotpool drains a bit.
ryan: Observability: p95 decreasing but still above SLA. Batching queue depth reduced by ~60%.
maria: Prod traffic: divert 15% to na1 as emergency lane to keep app-level latency under SLA. Command: `trafficctl shift --from eu-central --to na1 --filter 'tier==prod' --percentage 15`
infra-bot: Prod diversion executed: 15% of prod traffic diverted to na1.
oncall-lead: Keep diversion for 30m, monitor error budgets. If stable, we can slowly bring traffic back.
stefan: Postmortem TODOs added: revert k/v eviction heuristic change in runtime branch, add canary healthcheck for kv-attach under heavy queue, autoscaler tuning to avoid backoff on transient failures.
nina: Remaining actions: finish rollback (ETA 4m), confirm hotpool healthy, remove non-prod diversion, keep 15% prod diversion for 30m.
ryan: Also file cost estimate for emergency na1 usage (CC finance) — rough calc: ~6 extra A100-40h for 2h.
maria: Noted. I'll open a ticket and ping finance.
deploy-bot: rollback complete. runtime eu-central at v2.14.1.
infra-bot: eu-central hotpool utilization 74%, queue depth trending down, kv-eviction rate normalized.
oncall-lead: Thanks team. Keep me posted. Follow-up call in 30m if metrics don't return to baseline. :thumbsup:
nina: will post summary and timeline to #incidents after metrics stabilize. Thanks all for quick responses.
